text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS

- The prosecutor's office submitted to Prime Minister Andris Shkele the results of an investigation into a possible violation of the anti-corruption law by Juris Celmins, minister of education and science, and Juris Vinkelis, state minister of health care. The results will be made public this morning.
- Most party leaders are critical of the TV address made by Shkele, in which he criticised political parties.
- Parliament rejected the bill on a big rise in MPs salaries and pensions.
- Parliament rejected the motion of no confidence in Communications Minister Vilis Krishtopans.
- The first test-tube child was born in Latvia. A 33-year old woman gave birth to twin babies, a girl and a boy.
DIENA
- A U.S. artist of Latvian origin, Vija Celmina, won a prize of the U.S. MacArthur Foundation.
NEATKARIGA RITA AVIZE

- Foreign minister Valdis Birkavs reported on the results of his visit to the U.S. He hopes Secretary of State Madeleine Albright will visit Latvia by the end of this year. In June, a delegation of the U.S. State Departrment will arrive in Latvia to discuss the draft of the Baltic charter, an agreement between the U.S. and Latvia on security.
- VEF banka has been allowed to take deposits from individuals.
- Parliament passed a competition law, aimed at creating conditions for free and honest competition.
BIZNES I BALTIYA
- The constitution protection bureau is keeping secret the names of those who tried to blow up the Soviet-era Victory monument.
- The Isle of Man has complied with a demand by the liquidators of Banka Baltija that offshore companies Finhold, Julav and TAL, which have ties to the bankrupt bank, should be liquidated.
- Shares of Rakvere meat-packing plant, which recently bought a controlling stake in Rigas Miesnieks, were suspended on the bourse pending an insider dealing investigation.
- Parliament passed amendments to the law on the Bank of Latvia, under which the candidature of president is to be proposed by at least 10 MPs.
DIENAS BIZNESS
- Parliament passed amendments to the excise tax law, increasing excise duty per one litre of alcohol from 3.50 lats to 4 lats from July 1.
